t:
(a) There is authorized to be appropriated from the revenues of the District of Columbia not to exceed $50,000,000 to carry out the purposes of titles I and II of this Act. The authorization made by this subsection shall include any amounts made available pursuant to the amendment made by subsection (b) of this section. 
    (b) Subsection (b) of the first section of the Act approved June 6, 1958 (D.C. Code, sec. 9–220(b)), is amended—

        (1) 
by striking out “$250,000,000” in the first sentence and inserting in lieu thereof “$290,000,000”, and
 
        (2) 
by inserting immediately before the period at the end of the first sentence the following: “and (3) $40,000,000 of the principal amount of loans authorized to be advanced pursuant to this subsection shall be utilized to carry out the purposes of titles 1 and II of the District of Columbia Public Education Act”.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations from District of Columbia revenues and raises a loan ceiling to fund titles I and II of the Act. The tempting reading is that the mention of the District of Columbia signals coordination with a local government, but the District appears only as the source of funds. No consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is provided for any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: There is authorized to be appropriated from the revenues of the District of Columbia not to exceed $50,000,000 to carry out the purposes of titles I and II of this Act.

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes appropriations and amends funding limits for specific programs. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The text deals strictly with financial authorizations and statutory amendments regarding fund usage.
qwen_block.s: (a) There is authorized to be appropriated from the revenues of the District of Columbia not to exceed $50,000,000 to carry out the purposes of titles I and II of this Act.

opus.w: This section only authorizes funding and amends loan dollar limits. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Mentioning the District of Columbia and its education act concerns where the money comes from and what it is for. It does not involve outside parties in any federal decision.
opus.s: There is authorized to be appropriated from the revenues of the District of Columbia not to exceed $50,000,000 to carry out the purposes of titles I and II of this Act.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the reference to the "District of Columbia Public Education Act" and to loans being "advanced" suggests some outside involvement. That reading fails. The section only authorizes appropriations and changes loan dollar amounts. No outside party is consulted, there is no hearing, comment period, or rulemaking, and no one is given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section authorizes appropriations and amends loan limits for the District of Columbia. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the general public, states, or tribes) before making a decision. The text is purely fiscal and administrative.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for the "District of Columbia Public Education Act," this implies some form of public input or participation in educational decisions. However, the text itself only authorizes appropriations and amends loan limits. It does not describe any process for consulting with the public, states, or other outside entities. The District of Columbia is a federal district, and its government is generally considered part of the federal structure for these purposes, or at least the text does not specify any external consultation.
